title: RLT Fundraising Officer
description:
This is a hands-on role where you will have the opportunity to build your fundraising experience and make a

real contribution to the River Learning Trust’s (RLT) ability to increase funding for key educational priorities

and initiatives. You will also be helping to build the culture of philanthropy across the RLT community,

managing resources, administration, and communications across the network.

You will be pivotal in researching and applying for funding from grant-making bodies, and also supporting

the freelance fundraising consultant to build meaningful relationships with potential donors, local

businesses, and other stakeholder groups.

You will also be responsible for managing the day-to-day running and support of the Trust-wide CRM

fundraising database, Beacon, ensuring best practice, alongside developing, and supporting the user base

across the school network.

Working with our freelance fundraising consultant, and reporting into the Trust’s CFO, the medium- to long-

term goal is to ensure that the Trust continues to build a strong and dynamic fundraising community,

alongside increasing the amount of philanthropic income used to support important areas of educational

need.

What skills / experience are required

We’re looking for someone with at least one year’s experience in a fundraising role who is organised,

enthusiastic, and confident building relationships. We need someone who can work independently,

proactively, and to a high standard, but also enjoys working collaboratively with the rest of the team and

wider staff network. You need to understand and be demonstrably competent using a CRM database, and

other relevant software, as well as writing clear and engaging funding applications and communications.

What we can offer

You will have the opportunity to build your fundraising knowledge and skill-set, in a casual, yet supportive

environment, working alongside our experienced fundraising consultant, and other established fundraising

professionals across the network. The post-holder will be expected to develop and drive several important

projects over the medium- to long-term, and do so by working flexibly across the week, during term time.

Education has the power to change lives, communities, and society for the better. At RLT we believe that we

can achieve more for our pupils, trainees, staff, and communities by working together rather than alone.

Schools in RLT are united by a common belief in the benefits of working together, and by our commitment to

shared principles.

OUR VISION is for our schools and SCITT to improve rapidly, continuously, and sustainably: to be better

faster together.

OUR ‘WHY?’ is that children and young people ‘only get one go’ in school and therefore as part of RLT we

aim to ensure the best possible ‘go’ for our pupils.

OUR ‘HOW?’ is through the highest support and challenge for our schools and each other, underpinned by

our principles.

Our employees benefit from a wide variety of support including extensive continuing professional learning

and development opportunities, wellbeing and staff networks and access to Defined Benefit Pension

Schemes (TPS and LGPS) for all staff. ,For more information on what it is like to work for the Trust, and the

benefits you could access, please see our “Working in RLT” guide.

This role includes regulated activity relevant to children.

If you would like to have a confidential chat with Ali James about the role, prior to application, then please

email: ajames@riverlearningtrust.org, to arrange a call.

The River Learning Trust is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of all children and

preventing extremism. The Trust is required to conduct a variety of checks and online searches about you

as part of their recruitment process in accordance with Keeping Children Safe in Education guidance. It is an

 About the role

 We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer who can define and deliver products that have a real impact on people's financial futures. You'll be joining a small and early-stage engineering team where each engineer has significant ownership and your contributions will directly shape the product and the company's technical direction.

 As a senior member of our engineering team, you'll focus on the development and supporting infrastructure of vested.co – our core equity management and stock-option-funding platform.

 What You'll Do

• Build impactful features : Design and implement user-facing features that help people understand and manage their equity compensation.

• Own end-to-end delivery : Take projects from concept to production, including system design, implementation, testing, and deployment.

• Shape our technical direction : Contribute to architectural decisions and help establish engineering best practices as we scale.

• Collaborate cross-functionally : Work closely with product, design, and business teams to deliver exceptional user experiences.

• Grow the team : Share your expertise with other engineers and help build a culture of continuous learning. Help us grow and shape our inclusive, friendly, egoless engineering culture.

• Solve complex problems : Tackle challenging technical problems around financial calculations, data integrations, and building reliable systems at scale.

• 4+ years of software engineering experience with a track record of shipping production software.

• Full-stack capabilities with strong expertise in modern web technologies. We work with React, Next.js, TypeScript, and MongoDB. You should be experienced building frontend features, designing APIs, and modeling data relationships.

• Product mindset : You care deeply about user experience and enjoy building products that solve real problems.

• Strong communication skills : Ability to explain complex technical concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences.

• Ownership mentality : You take pride in your work and see projects through from start to finish.

• Growth mindset : Eager to learn new technologies and domains.

• Meaningful equity, with industry-leading grant terms (naturally)

 Location

 Fully remote. Standup and collaboration is centered mostly around the Eastern Time Zone, but we have team members from Alaska to Europe.

 Ready to Join Us?

 If you're excited about making equity ownership accessible to everyone and want to work on challenging technical problems with a real-world impact, we'd love to hear from you.

 Our interview process will include an initial meeting to assess mutual interest, a live technical interview, and further opportunities to meet the team and discuss your background.

 Please send a brief note expressing your interest as well as your resume to engineering@vested.co with the subject “Senior Software Engineer Application.”

 Vested is an equal opportunity employer and considers all quali fi ed applicants equally without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran status, or disability.

 We're headquartered in Denver, Colorado and we have offices and employees around the globe. We serve the largest, most demanding enterprises worldwide, including more than half of the Fortune 100.  Ping Identity is seeking a strategic, commercially minded, and highly influential Director, Global Alliances – Accenture to own and accelerate our relationship with Accenture worldwide.

 This is a high-impact global leadership role—not a regional partner-management position. You will serve as Ping’s single accountable alliance leader for Accenture, shaping the global strategy, executive relationship, operating model, and joint go-to-market plan across Accenture’s Identity, Security, Technology, Song, industry, cloud, delivery, and managed-services organizations.

 The successful candidate will turn a complex global relationship into a focused, repeatable growth engine—aligning executives, mobilizing Ping’s teams, and helping Accenture make Ping the identity platform of choice in strategic transformation programs.

 This is a hands-on builder role. You will craft the strategy, create the operating model, and drive execution from executive alignment through customer outcomes. You will build top-down and bottoms-up engagement and convert shared priorities into strategic collaboration agreements, joint investment plans, and measurable results.

 What you will own

 Global alliance strategy and executive leadership

• Define and execute a multi-year global Accenture alliance strategy aligned to Ping’s corporate priorities, growth objectives, product strategy, and regional plans.

• Establish trusted relationships with Accenture’s global and regional executives across Identity, Cybersecurity, Technology, Song, cloud, industry, delivery, and managed services.

• Act as Ping’s primary global Accenture leadership point and orchestrate executive alignment when priorities, resources, commercial interests, or customer pursuits require senior intervention.

• Build and maintain a joint annual business plan with clear priorities, investments, owners, milestones, and measurable outcomes.

• Create a global-to-local operating model that gives AMER, EMEA, and APJ teams a common strategy while allowing appropriate regional and country-level activation.

• Drive GTM Acceleration, ensuring Ping is front-and-center with Accenture SAL’s and CAL’s across industry verticals.

 Strategic engagement and collaboration agreements

• Build a deliberate, multi-threaded engagement model with Accenture’s global leadership, practice executives, industry leaders, regional sponsors, account executives, and delivery leaders.

• Create executive alignment around a small number of strategic priorities, including the business case, mutual value, investment requirements, customer outcomes, and path to scale.

• Develop, advance, and operationalize strategic collaboration agreements, memoranda of understanding, annual business plans, and related partnership frameworks with Accenture.

• Translate agreements into clear gives-and-gets, governance structures, named owners, investment principles, milestones, escalation paths, and measurable success criteria.

• Partner with Ping Finance, Legal, Operations, Product, Sales, Sales Engineering, Professional Services, and executive leadership to ensure agreements are commercially sound, executable, and connected to Ping’s broader strategy.

• Establish a cadence of executive briefings, steering committees, business reviews, and working sessions that keeps both organizations aligned and accountable.

• Identify when a relationship should progress from informal collaboration to a formal strategic agreement, and lead the internal and partner process required to make that progression successful.

 Joint go-to-market and revenue growth

• Develop a disciplined joint go-to-market motion spanning “to,” “with,” and “through” Accenture partner routes.

• Build and manage a prioritized target-account strategy, including account mapping, install-base intelligence, whitespace analysis, opportunity hypotheses, and executive sponsorship.

• Mobilize Ping account teams and Accenture sales, account, industry, and practice leaders around qualified opportunities and strategic pursuits.

• Drive partner-sourced, partner-influenced, co-sell, resale, services-attach, and expansion revenue while establishing clear definitions for attribution and credit.

• Create repeatable joint offers and sales plays that connect Ping’s identity security platform with Accenture’s consulting, implementation, transformation, and managed-services capabilities.

• Improve pipeline quality, progression, forecast accuracy, win rates, deal velocity, and strategic account penetration through consistent inspection and action planning.

 Governance, operating rhythm, and accountability

  • We are part of the Cycle to Work scheme. Tax free bikes and safety equipment can be payable by payroll deduction through a partnership with Cyclescheme.
  • Free parking

Applications are invited from enthusiastic and highly motivated individuals who are able to work as part of the whole staff team, and who will support and uphold the Catholic ethos and practices of the school.

Important - Please refer to the Definition of a Practising Catholic document for full details before submitting your application.

All Saints is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people. Therefore, we expect all workers, volunteers and employees to share this commitment. A conviction may not exclude candidates from appointment but will be considered as part of the recruitment process.

title: Salesforce Lead - USA
description:
Headquarters: Remote

 Storyblok is a headless CMS that enables marketers and developers to create with joy and publish with confidence. It empowers you to deliver structured and consistent content everywhere: websites, apps, AI search, and beyond.

 Legendary brands like Virgin Media O2, Oatly, and TomTom use Storyblok to make a bigger, faster market impact.

 WHAT IS IN IT FOR YOU

 You will be joining a growing company where you can contribute to many “firsts”. Plus these benefits:

• Monthly remote work stipend (home internet costs, electricity). Home office equipment package right at the start (laptop, keyboard, monitor…)

• Home office equipment upgrade (furniture, ear plugs …) or membership to a local co-working space after your onboarding

• Sick leave benefit, parental leave and 25 days of annual leave plus your local national holidays

• Personal development fund for courses, books, conferences, and material

• The annual international team-building trip, quarterly and monthly online get-togethers

• As a fully remote company, with work-life balance at its core, you’ll enjoy flexible schedules

• An international team that loves to have fun at work and works hard together to accomplish shared goals

 JOB SUMMARY

 Storyblok is hiring a Salesforce Lead to own Salesforce architecture, execution, governance, data quality, integrations, and release discipline across our GTM workflows. This techno-functional owner moves from business process to system design, build coordination, release control, data quality, reporting impact, and user adoption, owning Sales Cloud and core CRM objects, Pardot / Account Engagement, DealHub CPQ integration, lead-to-cash and quote-to-cash workflows, routing, campaign and lifecycle data, permissions, integrations, and documentation. The role also leads future platform evaluation for Salesforce Data 360, Salesforce Marketing Cloud Advanced, Adobe Marketing Cloud, Oracle Responsys, and related CDP needs, and, if a platform is selected, leads implementation planning and execution with RevOps, Marketing Operations, Data, Finance, Legal, vendors, and external partners.

 ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS

• Salesforce architecture and GTM systems governance

• Own Salesforce platform architecture across GTM workflows, objects, fields, permissions, automations, integrations, and release control.

• Translate RevOps, Marketing Operations, Sales, Customer Success, Finance, and Data requirements into clean system design and controlled execution.

• Maintain governance for new fields, objects, flows, validation rules, permission sets, integrations, reporting dependencies, and documentation.

• Sales Cloud and core CRM ownership

• Own system design for leads, contacts, accounts, opportunities, activities, campaigns, lifecycle stages, routing, renewals, expansions, and customer handoffs.

• Support lead-to-cash workflows with clear ownership, required fields, source logic, stage rules, assignment logic, and adoption checks.

• Monitor CRM completeness, data freshness, duplicates, routing failures, and workflow friction that creates manual workarounds.

• Pardot, Account Engagement, and marketing workflow support

• Partner with Marketing Operations on Pardot or Account Engagement, campaign data, lifecycle stages, scoring inputs, consent, routing, attribution support, and funnel reporting.

• Maintain the Salesforce-side architecture for marketing-to-sales handoffs, campaign member data, source fields, conversion logic, and reporting quality.

• Keep current marketing workflows stable while future marketing cloud and CDP options are evaluated.

• Future Data 360, SFMC Advanced, Adobe, Oracle, and CDP evaluation

• Lead the requirements, scorecard, architecture review, vendor comparison, data governance review, and implementation readiness plan for future customer data and marketing cloud decisions.

• Evaluate Salesforce Data 360, Salesforce Marketing Cloud Advanced, Adobe Marketing Cloud, Oracle Responsys, and related CDP needs against GTM use cases, data model, activation, consent, reporting, integration, cost, and operating complexity.

• If a platform is selected, lead implementation planning and execution with clear phases, owners, risks, testing, migration, enablement, and adoption metrics.

• DealHub CPQ integration, data quality, releases, and adoption

• Own Salesforce-side integration quality for DealHub CPQ, including quote data, approval sync, product lines, opportunity fields, order handoffs, and reporting impact.

• Run release management with intake, solution design, testing, regression checks, deployment, communication, documentation, and adoption tracking.

• Partner with Data on source-to-report logic so Salesforce, warehouse, Finance, and leadership reporting stay aligned.

 EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

• Bachelor's degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, Business, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

• 6+ years in the Salesforce ecosystem, including hands-on administration and solution / architecture ownership in a GTM or Revenue Operations context.

• Salesforce certifications strongly preferred (e.g., Administrator, Advanced Administrator, Platform App Builder; Sales Cloud Consultant or Application Architect a plus).

• Hands-on experience with Sales Cloud, core CRM objects, declarative automation (Flow), permissions, and release / change management across environments.

• Experience with Pardot / Marketing Cloud Account Engagement and marketing-to-sales workflows, and with CPQ tools (DealHub or comparable) across lead-to-cash and quote-to-cash.

• Experience integrating Salesforce with downstream systems (data warehouse, Finance, marketing, order management) and supporting reporting and data quality.

• Familiarity with CDP / marketing cloud platform evaluation (e.g., Salesforce Data 360, SFMC Advanced, Adobe, Oracle Responsys) is a plus.

• Demonstrates AI literacy, with the ability to leverage AI tools to enhance productivity, decision-making, and quality of work while applying sound judgment and critical thinking.

 PROFESSIONAL COMPETENCIES

• Systems thinking: translates cross-functional business requirements into clean, scalable system design and governance.

• Technical CRM depth: strong command of Salesforce architecture, data model, automation, permissions, and integrations.

• Release and change discipline: structured intake, testing, regression, deployment, documentation, and adoption tracking.

• Data quality and governance orientation: drives completeness, freshness, deduplication, and field control.

• Stakeholder management: partners effectively across RevOps, Marketing Operations, Sales, CS, Finance, Data, Legal, and vendors.

• Vendor and platform evaluation: builds requirements, scorecards, and implementation readiness plans for major platform decisions.

• Clear communication: explains what is being built, the decision needed, and the business outcome to technical and non-technical audiences.

• Bias for reliability: reduces defects, manual workarounds, and ambiguity through documentation and controlled execution.

 U.S. Base Salary Range: $102,900 - $140,000

We consider many factors when it comes to compensation, such as the scope of the role, job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. Our base salary ranges are determined by job and job level and are benchmarked to relevant location and industry data. The range displayed represents the target US base compensation range within which we are hiring for this role. For some roles Storyblok also offers a competitive commission structure.

 Storyblok has a commitment to diversity and inclusion. We strive to create a hiring environment in which all people feel they are equally respected and valued, irrespective of gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, ethnicity, age, religion, citizenship or any other characteristic. You can find more information about our privacy policy here .

description:
Our Trust

At the heart of our Catholic Multi-Academy Trust is a mission that shapes everything we do. Inspired by the witness of St Gabriel the Archangel, we are Forming Christ-centred pilgrims of hope with kind hearts, questioning minds, a thirst for knowledge, and a hunger for justice. These characteristics are lived out in our schools, they shape our culture, leadership, teaching, and our community. St Gabriel the Archangel Catholic Multi-Academy Trust is a family of 64 schools working together to provide high-quality, faith-filled education to every child we serve.

About this Role

St Mary’s Catholic Primary School, Brewood, is a welcoming and inclusive school with a warm, supportive atmosphere, open to families of all faiths. We are committed to high standards in wellbeing, behaviour, and personal development, alongside a strong community ethos and enriching opportunities for every child. As part of St Gabriel the Archangel Catholic Multi-Academy Trust, we provide a nurturing environment where children—and staff—can thrive.

We are looking for a dedicated and compassionate 1:1 Teaching Assistant to join our team.

The successful candidate will provide support to pupils, helping them engage with the curriculum, develop their skills and build confidence in a positive, nurturing and inclusive environment.

We are looking for someone who is patient, caring and enthusiastic, with a genuine commitment to supporting children and helping them achieve their full potential.

Required to start as soon as possible!

32.5 hours per week, Monday to Friday, term-time only plus INSETS

About the Role:

Working closely with the class teacher, SENDCO and wider school team, you will provide individual support to help the child access learning, participate in classroom activities and develop greater independence.

Key responsibilities will include:

  • Providing tailored 1:1 support to meet the child’s individual learning and developmental needs.
  • Supporting the child to access the curriculum and engage in learning activities.

  • Working collaboratively with colleagues and following agreed strategies to support the child’s progress.
  • Promoting a safe, inclusive and caring learning environment in which every child feels supported and valued.

The ideal candidate will be:

  • Caring, patient, approachable and nurturing.
  • Enthusiastic about supporting children’s learning and development.
  • Able to build positive, trusting relationships with children.
  • Calm, flexible and proactive in responding to individual needs.
  • A good communicator who works effectively as part of a team.
  • Committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children.
  • Supportive of the ethos and values of our Catholic school.

Previous experience in a primary school or working with children with additional needs would be an advantage.

What We Can Offer:

We provide a supportive and friendly working environment where you will be a valued member of our close-knit school community. You will have opportunities for training and professional development, enjoy a competitive salary and benefits, and work in a safe and welcoming workplace.

Apply Today:
Join a welcoming, close-knit community where every day is an opportunity to make a positive difference.

title: Estates Manager
description:
CORE Education Trust is a values-driven multi-academy trust rich in cultural and social diversity. Responsible for four academies in Birmingham, the Trust was set up to innovate through adversity and to challenge the conventional boundaries of what is possible for our students. Motivated and inspired by the success of our students, our ambition goes beyond textbooks and whiteboards, we are proud to work with the young people of Birmingham.

This role will be based at CORE Education Trust which is an 11-16 co-educational school. You will be joining an academy team whose sole aim is to ensure that all students get the very best support, care and guidance that enables them to achieve their very best.

WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR?

Our school is a place of possibility and we never underestimate the impact inspirational staff can have on the life chances of our students. We are seeking a dynamic Estates Manager who can demonstrate their commitment to driving up standards, expectations, and aspirations, so that staff and students regularly experience success and a sense of progression, whilst acting as a role model for staff within the department.

The successful candidate should be committed to improving the lives of the young people at CORE Education Trust.

WHAT WE OFFER

The successful candidate will be joining a vibrant learning community with national award-winning credentials. The Trust works collaboratively with leaders to ensure our CORE Values are promoted, embodied, and celebrated by all the staff and children in our schools. You will:

  • be given the opportunity to engage with cross-trust activities that connect students and staff to their wider family of schools/peers across the city. This includes programmes such as the award-winning Echo Eternal Holocaust memorial arts initiative and The COREus Choir.
  • be provided with a provision of support and training to foster a positive culture of wellbeing for all students and staff.

We place a strong emphasis on supporting and encouraging personal development, which includes:

  • a CPD strategy that is designed to support the career aspirations of all staff to help them realise their potential.
  • access to experienced mentors who have a strong track record of developing staff.

This is an exciting time to join the trust. We have a well-established outward facing ethos as a forward thinking family of schools guided by a vision underpinned by optimism, ambition and oneness.

title: Assistant Educational Psychologist
description:
Be part of something ambitious. Help every child thrive

Bridge Academy Trust (BAT) is seeking to appoint a 2 year fixed term Assistant Educational Psychologist to join our expanding Inclusion offer. This is a rare opportunity to gain broad, purposeful experience across a family of highly collaborative schools that place inclusion, belonging and opportunity at the heart of everything they do. Working across primary, secondary and specialist resource base provision, you will play a key role in helping children and young people overcome barriers, develop confidence and achieve success.

You will contribute to the development of an innovative Trust wide model of psychological support, working alongside passionate and experienced school leaders. This is a genuine step towards doctoral training as an Educational Psychologist.

You will work under the professional supervision of a qualified Educational Psychologist, with dedicated CPD and supervision arrangements provided by Essex County Council, giving you the structure and support of a Local Authority EP service alongside the pace and variety of a multi-academy trust.

Why join us

  • Breadth of experience across primary, secondary and specialist resource base provision — rare for an Assistant EP post.
  • The opportunity to work alongside an exceptional network of experienced SENDCos and inclusion leaders.
  • Professional supervision and CPD provided by Essex County Council, alongside day-to-day support from the Trust.
  • A genuinely varied caseload: early intervention work, EHCNA-related assessment, small group intervention, and staff training.
  • The chance to help shape a Trust-wide model of psychological support from the ground up, working closely with school leaders and SENDCos.
  • A supportive, ambitious Trust with a strong track record of school improvement and inclusive practice.

You will be deployed flexibly across BAT's schools rather than fixed to a single site, working alongside qualified Educational Psychologists to:

  • Carry out targeted individual observation, advice and guidance to support in-school provision ahead of an Education, Health and Care Needs Assessment (EHCNA).
  • Undertake individual observation and write-up to support the EHCNA process, feeding into EP psychological advice.
  • Deliver small group intervention work directly with pupils.
  • Contribute to staff training on specific areas of development, such as adaptive teaching strategies for identified pupils or groups and to the development of evidence-based, best practice for inclusive provision.

About you:

  • A psychology degree (2:1 or above), an approved conversion course, or a Master's degree, AND eligibility for British Psychological Society (BPS) Graduate Basis for Chartered Membership (GBC).
  • Experience of working with children and young people in an education, care or family-oriented setting.
  • A genuine commitment to applying psychology to support children and young people with Special Educational Needs and/or Disabilities (SEND).
  • Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with high personal and professional integrity.
  • A self-driven, reflective approach, with the confidence to work autonomously and know when to seek support.

Please read the job description before applying. A driving license and access to your own vehicle is essential for this role due to location changes.

Bridge Academy Trust may close this advert early if we receive a high volume of suitable applications.

title: Lunchbreak Supervisor
description:
Job title: Lunchbreak Supervisor 

Working hours: 10 per week 

Working pattern: 12.30pm - 2.30pm, Monday - Friday

Working weeks: 38 weeks per year (term time only) 

Salary: £13.07 per hour (PATH 1) 

Location: The King Alfred School 


Our Lunchbreak Supervisors play a vital role in creating a safe, happy and well-organised lunchtime experience for our pupils. Each role involves working 2 hours per day during the lunch period.


About the role 

We’re looking for a caring and enthusiastic Lunchbreak Supervisor to join our school team and help make lunchtimes a positive part of every student's day. You’ll work closely with staff and pupils to create a safe, sociable and well organised environment. 

You will:

  • Supervise students during lunchtime in dining areas, outdoor spaces and corridors to maintain safety and good behaviour.
  • Ensure students follow school rules, including proper conduct during meals, in queues, and in designated areas.
  • Help keep the dining area clean by tidying up spillages and assisting with litter picking during and after the lunch break.


About you 

You’ll be someone who brings warmth, energy and a sense of fun to the role. We’re looking for someone who is:

  • Flexible, calm, and well-organised
  • Able to take initiative and work confidently as part of a team
  • Sensitive to the needs of all children
  • Approachable, with strong communication skills
  • Experienced in working with children in a supervisory role 

We can offer you:

  • Happy, engaging students who thrive on inspirational leadership
  • A supportive trust and school community
  • Strong collaboration across the trust family of schools and access to a centralised team of specialists across all areas of school operations
  • A commitment to high‑quality CPD, with dedicated time and budget for your development
  • A values‑driven ethos where diversity, equity and inclusion are lived every day
  • Recognition of continuous service (modification order) to protect employment rights and entitlements
  • Local Government Pension Scheme with generous employer contributions and death‑in‑service cover
  • Occupational sick pay to support you during illness or unexpected emergencies
  • Family‑friendly leave packages to help maintain a healthy work–life balance


In order to apply for this role please complete an application form by 9am, Friday 6th November. Please let us know if you require any adjustments as part of the process. 


Please know that depending on the number of applications received we may decide to close the advert early. If you do not hear from us by a week after the closing date then please assume that you have not been shortlisted for an interview. If you have previously applied for this role there is no requirement to apply again, all applications will be reviewed. We wish you all the best in your future and ask that you join our E-Teach Talent Pool so as to keep up to date with all of our latest current opportunities. 


Join us in Providing a Great Education for Every Child 

Pathway Trust is committed to equal opportunities and encourages applicants from all backgrounds and communities, as we recognise the importance and benefit this has for our pupils.

title: Estates Maintenance Officer
description:
Please note that there is some flexibility in terms of hours for this position.

Job Title - Estates Maintenance Officer

About You

Are you looking to make a hands-on, positive impact in a supportive school community? Do you bring genuine enthusiasm for working in an educational environment where your daily efforts directly benefit our students?

Whether you are an experienced tradesperson, a skilled maintenance professional, or someone with strong practical aptitude eager to learn and grow, we want to hear from you. We are looking for someone who takes deep pride in keeping our facilities running safely, smoothly, and sustainably.

If you want to join an organisation where Estates staff are recognised as essential partners in our success, where your growth is backed by funded formal apprenticeship qualifications, and where staff are always treated people first, this is the place for you.


The Role

As an Estates Maintenance Officer, you will join a dedicated site and support team at The Oxford Academy, playing a pivotal role in creating a safe, clean, and inspiring environment where our students can thrive every day.

We are open to applications from individuals with varying levels of experience:

  • Experienced Candidates: You bring established skills in site management, health and safety compliance, practical DIY, or building maintenance trades.

  • Less Experienced Candidates: You bring a strong practical mindset, a proactive attitude, and the enthusiasm to develop your craft through structured support and CPLD pathways..

Why This Role Matters

At The Oxford Academy, our Estates team does far more than maintain buildings - you help shape the physical heartbeat of our school. By keeping our grounds safe, welcoming, and well-cared for, you directly enable high-quality learning and help foster a sense of pride across our entire community. We genuinely value this role as a cornerstone of our day-to-day success.


Why Join Us

This is an important time to join The Oxford Academy, where our values of ‘commitment to others, commitment to learning’ drive everything we do. We are seeking a skilled individual who shares our deep belief that education has the power to transform lives, communities, and society for the better.

You will be joining a team where staff are genuinely proud of the work they do, recognising how valuable a high-quality education is for improving pupils' life chances, and remain very positive about working at the school (Ofsted 2026).

At The Oxford Academy, support staff are valued as essential professional partners in our school's success. We actively invest in our team through CPLD and formal apprenticeship pathways funded via the River Learning Trust Apprenticeship Levy. Whether you are starting out or looking to broaden your career, our support staff have successfully completed Level 3 to Level 5 qualifications, enabling meaningful internal career progression.

Shaping Futures and Long-Term Success

Continued Professional Development

‘With the Trust's support and the Apprenticeship Levy, I completed both a Level 5 Operations Management apprenticeship and a Level 5 CIPD qualification. That structured CPLD provided the foundation to move into HR; a shift made possible by RLT’s commitment to internal professional development’ (Manager, The Oxford Academy).

Community and Connection

‘I am delighted to have joined TOA. I have felt consistently supported by my line manager, Nora Ward, as well as the Senior Leadership, Central teams and HR colleagues. From day one, it was clear that this is an environment where I can build effective systems, grow professionally, and see the real-world impact of my work. It’s a privilege to be part of a community that truly lives its values; placing students at the heart of everything while ensuring staff feel respected and genuinely valued’ (Manager, The Oxford Academy).

‘The atmosphere at The Oxford Academy is truly like no other, it is a space that is as inspiring as it is motivating. There is an infectious energy here driven by a staff and students that fills me with pride. I’ve reached a point where I feel like a stick of rock, I am TOA through and through’ (Senior Leader, The Oxford Academy).

Care and Compassion

‘What I didn't expect, though, was to find an environment where the differing strengths of each and every staff member are valued and that time would be invested in me to be the best I could be. I ventured through a number of roles and, since I retired from teaching, I have continued in a support role that enables me to make a difference.

One other thing that should be highlighted is that staff are thought of as people, and not work units. I suffered a bout of serious ill-health and the TOA family supported me in my return to the chalkface, and I will be forever grateful to them’ (Administrator, The Oxford Academy).

‘Being part of creating successful futures for so many students is something that I will always be proud of. My enthusiasm grows for my job every single day’ (Intervention Tutor, The Oxford Academy).

Flexibility

While this position is advertised as full time, we warmly consider requests for part-time hours or flexible working arrangements. Please indicate your preference on the application form.

Our School

At The Oxford Academy, we offer pride, aspiration, and opportunity to every member of our community, with significantly improved learning outcomes. We are committed to ensuring that our students and staff are highly successful through sustainable, positive improvements in our school.

Do you want to work in a school that:

  • Is friendly and community-centred, where staff genuinely feel part of a team?

  • Utilises a new teaching approach that has "helped to dramatically improve both pupils' behaviour and participation in lessons. As a result, lessons are undisturbed, and pupils enjoy their learning" (Ofsted 2026).

  • Places staff well-being at the heart of everything we do.

  • Employs a full-time Instructional Coach who works with staff to develop practice through specific teaching goals that maximise student learning.

  • Benefits from a culture where "behaviour across the school is now very positive. Pupils are calm and respectful, with positive attitudes to learning" (Ofsted 2026).

  • Prioritises high-quality bespoke CPLD, supporting staff to gain formal qualifications and apprenticeships via the RLT Apprenticeship Levy and providing collaboration opportunities across a successful and highly respected multi-academy trust.

Community and Connection

The Oxford Academy is an important part of our local community, and we actively encourage individuals from our area—including parents of our students and residents in our neighborhood—to join our team. We believe that being part of a community goes far beyond our physical location; it is about fostering genuine connections, understanding, and mutual support. By investing in local talent, we ensure that our school's values align closely with the daily needs and aspirations of the families we serve.

Many of our team members have deep local roots, including staff who attended the school themselves and have worked here for decades:

‘I have worked at The Oxford Academy for 26 years, having also attended this school as a pupil when it was Peers. Being part of creating successful futures for so many students is something I will always be proud of’ (Long-serving TOA Staff Member).

At our school, we want everyone to feel safe, valued, and respected—not just in theory, but in practice. We are fully committed to creating an inclusive environment where everyone feels they truly belong. Our community deeply embraces its unique character; as noted by inspectors, "pupils are proud of the school's very diverse character, and they appreciate the way they are taught about respect and positive behaviour" (Ofsted 2026). This intentional focus ensures that "pupils are happy in school. They feel known and liked by their teachers. This helps to build the school's sense of cohesion and belonging" (Ofsted 2026).

When you join us, you are not just becoming part of our internal school family; you are joining an organisation that actively cares for and remains a pillar of the local community. We would love to hear from applicants from all diverse backgrounds who share this profound commitment to inclusion.

Employee Benefits

Health & Wellbeing

  • Free annual flu vaccines

  • Discounted gym memberships (onsite gym)

  • Access to an Employee Assistance Programme

  • 24-hour access to a free counselling helpline (including family and debt advice)

  • Flexible working solutions

  • Reduced teaching time

  • Onsite nursery provision through Little Peeple Nursery

Financial

  • Local Government Pension Scheme (LGPS), with employee contributions of 19.2%

  • Eligible for a Blue Light Card - Hundreds of offers/discounts on local and national stores

  • Cycle to Work Scheme

  • The Oxford Academy sits outside the ring road and is less affected than other schools by the new Oxford Congestion Charge

Career Progression

  • Opportunities for CPLD and access to apprenticeships

  • Developmental performance management conversations

  • Apprenticeship opportunities for ‘on the job training’

  • Investment in your career, internal and external talent solutions

The River Learning Trust

At RLT, we believe we achieve more together than alone. Our schools are united by shared principles, collaboration, and a belief in the power of education to change lives.

Our Vision: for our schools and SCITT to improve rapidly, continuously, and sustainably — to be better faster together.

Our ‘Why’: children and young people only get one go at school — we aim to ensure it’s the best possible one.

Our ‘How’: through the highest support and challenge for each other, underpinned by shared principles.

Employees benefit from extensive continuing professional learning, strong wellbeing and staff networks, and access to Defined Benefit Pension Schemes (TPS and LGPS). For more information, see our “Working in RLT” guide.

Safeguarding and Recruitment

The River Learning Trust and The Oxford Academy are committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of all children and preventing extremism. The Trust is required to conduct a variety of checks and online searches about you as part of their recruitment process in accordance with Keeping Children Safe in Education guidance. It is an offence to apply for certain roles within schools if you are barred from engaging in regulated activity relevant to children.

For all RLT Safer Recruitment Documentation candidates should click on the following link RLT Safer Recruitment Documents for Candidates. Please see our website for up to date policies including our Child Protection and Behaviour Policies.

This post is exempt from the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974 and the amendments to the Exceptions Order 1975, 2013 and 2020. For further guidance for applicants click on this link List of offences that are not filtered

Next Steps

We encourage interested candidates to visit the school before applying. To arrange a visit, please contact Reception: enquiries@theoxfordacademy.org . For more information about The Oxford Academy, please visit our website.

Final Note

LEADERSHIP AND SUPERVISION

ADDITIONAL

title: Cover Supervisor
description:
Job Title: Cover Supervisor

Salary range: Scale 4 and spinal point 7 £29, 651 to spinal point 11 £31, 448 Inc. London weighting per annum (Pro rata £21, 049 - £22, 325)

Contract: Permanent

Start date: December 2026

Hours of work: 29.75 hours per week

Working weeks: 39 weeks

Location: Alperton, London

Aspire | Commit | Succeed

We are a split-site school, with a short walk of approximately 8 minutes between sites, and on-site parking is available.

Alperton Community School is a large, mixed 11-18 academy, with over 350 students in our thriving Sixth Form. Due to our growing popularity and continued success, we have recently expanded our intake to 12 forms in each year group.

We are a truly inclusive school, reflecting the wonderfully diverse and vibrant local community we serve. Our students are exceptionally well behaved, hardworking, and ambitious to succeed. In our most recent Ofsted inspection (March 2026), the school was graded Strong standard and Expected standard, with inspectors noting:

  • “Pupils enjoy attending this diverse and inclusive school. They feel a strong sense of belonging, which is evident in the positive relationships they have with staff and with each other.”
  • “Pupils are kept safe and they know whom to talk to if they have any concerns.”

Student progress at both GCSE and A Level has consistently been well above national averages. Outcomes for disadvantaged students closely match those of their peers. In 2023, our Progress 8 score was 0.82 (well above average), and our A Level progress placed us in the top 1% of schools nationally. A high proportion of our students go on to study at Oxbridge and other Russell Group universities.

Attendance across the school is excellent, and the percentage of students continuing into education, employment or training is significantly above the national average.

Our achievements have been recognised with several recent accolades, including the 2022 Pearson Making a Difference Award. We were also shortlisted for the TES School of the Year and won the TES Maths Team of the Year.

This is an exceptional opportunity to join a friendly, highly supportive, and committed team within a culture of success and professional growth. The school offers outstanding support for Early Career Teachers during their induction year.

We are a split-site school, with a short walk of approximately 8 minutes between sites, and on-site parking is available.

The Role

Cover Supervisor work is excellent experience for those looking to get into the teaching profession or to gain further experience in working with children. We value our staff and provide continuous professional development and Cover Supervisors are included in Alperton’s professional development programme alongside teaching staff. There are also additional opportunities to develop specific areas to support effectiveness in the role. Any time not spent covering lessons will be used for duties relating to the school development plan.

As a Cover Supervisor you will be required to provide effective classroom cover for students aged 11-16 in the absence of the main subject teacher and in line with the Alperton expectations for the quality of teaching and learning.

Your day will involve using the in-house procedures to access cover work and dealing with any immediate problems or emergencies according to the school’s policies/procedures. You will also contribute to the vast array of the school’s extra-curricular activities we offer to our students across all year groups.

The Person

We are looking for a dedicated and enthusiastic individual to join our support staff team—someone who is committed to helping students thrive and who enjoys working as part of a collaborative and supportive environment.

The ideal candidate will have:

  • A genuine passion for supporting young people in their learning and development
  • A commitment to inclusive, student-focused education
  • A flexible, proactive, and positive attitude
  • The ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team

This is a fantastic opportunity to play a key role in the daily life of the school and to make a real difference in the lives of our students.

The successful candidate will be a proactive individual with a ‘can-do’ attitude who is able to provide engaging and interesting lessons from work set by absent teachers. They do not need to specialise in any particular subject area but a high level of literacy and numeracy are essential for this role. If you are passionate about young people’s education, hardworking, flexible and a forward thinking individual who has good organisational skills and is looking for an exciting new challenge which is highly rewarding, then this role is perfect for you.

What We Offer

As part of our commitment to staff wellbeing and development, we offer a comprehensive benefits package, including:

  • Extensive CPD and professional growth opportunities
  • Employee Assistance Programme
  • Cashback Health Benefits
  • Cycle to Work Scheme
  • Pension Scheme
  • Opportunities for progression and leadership

Key Dates

Closing Date: 8 November 2026 (23:59)

Assessment & Interview Date: Week commencing, 9 November 2026

Supplementary Information

Applicants who have applied for this post in the last 6 months need not apply.

We are committed to safer recruitment and to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people, and expect all staff and volunteers to share this commitment. We welcome applications from all sections of the community.

The successful candidate(s) will be required to undertake an Enhanced and Barred Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check and register the DBS on the Update Service.

Please note: CVs will not be considered as part of your application.

Applicants may be contacted for a brief pre-screening call as part of our interview process to assess their suitability for the role.

Only successful candidates will be notified. If you do not hear from us within 14 days of the closing date, please assume you have not been successful on this occasion.

title: Behaviour Support Officer
description:
About Us

Furze Platt Senior School is a highly successful and inclusive mixed comprehensive school, with a strong commitment to student wellbeing, achievement and support.

We are seeking to appoint a Behaviour Support Officer to join our team from January 2027, or earlier if possible. Working as part of our wider Pastoral Team, you will be one of three Behaviour Support Officers, helping to promote positive behaviour, support student engagement and ensure a safe and supportive learning environment for all.

The role will involve a varied range of responsibilities, including managing our internal isolation room, supporting after-school detentions and assisting with behaviour interventions across the school, working closely with both students and staff.

The Role

As a Behaviour Support Officer, you will play a key role in supporting students who need additional behavioural guidance and academic focus. You will manage the isolation room, providing students with a calm space to reflect and reset, and support the running of daily after-school detentions. Additionally, you will work closely with teachers to respond to behavioural issues in classrooms and around the school, offering intervention and guidance to help maintain a positive learning environment.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Managing the isolation room and helping students reflect and reset to re-engage with learning.

  • Supporting students and staff during daily after-school detentions, ensuring students complete work in a structured environment.

  • Responding to behavioural incidents in classrooms and across the school site as part of the SLT call-out system.

  • Conducting investigations into behavioural issues and reporting to the Senior Leadership Team (SLT).

  • Rotating between managing the isolation room, providing call-out support, and assisting with behaviour interventions.

About You:

We are looking for individuals with strong interpersonal skills, patience, and the ability to remain calm under pressure. You should have experience working with young people, preferably in an educational setting, and the ability to build positive relationships with students, staff, and parents. A commitment to supporting students’ academic and personal development is essential.

Why Join Us?

At Furze Platt, we offer a supportive and friendly working environment with access to professional development opportunities. Staff benefits include access to an on-site gym, a comprehensive employee assistance program, and free on-site parking.

title: Deployment Strategist, Internship - Warp Speed
description:
A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.


What We're About
 
At its core, the Deployment Strategist role centers around using data in operational and real-world action. Our customers come to us with a hunch that the only way to protect their troops, manufacture high-quality products, structure effective healthcare policies, or deliver aid to refugees safely is to make better use of their data. Deployment Strategists are responsible for turning that hunch into reality.
 
The Role
 
Warp Speed builds on years of excellence in manufacturing to resurrect & revitalize the American Industrial Base. The Warp Speed Deployment role centers around using data in operational and real-world action. Our customers come to us with a hunch that the only way to manufacture high-quality products is to make better use of their data. Deployment Strategists are responsible for turning that hunch into a reality.
 
As a Deployment Strategist, you'll work as part of a driven and creative team of Engineers, Product Designers, and other Deployment Strategists to deploy software against the most exciting problems our world faces. Your mission is to synthesize disconnected streams of thought into an understanding of what the most important problem is, what the data means, what the product needs, what users are motivated by, and where the impact could be.
 
You'll immerse yourself in our customers' most intricate workflows. You'll partner with customer teams and explore the data, and plunge into the product landscape to enable us to scale. A select number of Deployments Strategists may also be deployed to Palantir internal teams and problems. In this role, the problems you'll seek will require a curious and analytical approach, a sharp intuition for product, and a strong degree of user insight to ultimately empower our customers to improve decisions.

title: Forward Deployed Software Engineer, Internship - Warp Speed
description:
A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.


The Role
 
Warp Speed
Warp Speed builds on years of excellence in manufacturing to resurrect & revitalize the American Industrial Base. FDSEs on Warp Speed work directly with customers from the factory floor to the board room to understand their greatest problems and design and implement solutions using data.
 
As Forward Deployed Software Engineers (FDSEs) you’ll apply your problem solving ability, creativity, and technical skills to help organizations use their data to drive a real impact in the world. You’ll have the opportunity to gain rare insight into and contribute to some of the most important industries and institutions globally!
 
The Original Forward Deployed Software Engineer 
At Palantir, the Forward Deployed Software Engineer (FDSE) role isn’t just a job title: it’s the blueprint. We pioneered this unique position, embedding talented engineers directly with our customers to tackle their most pressing challenges head-on. As an FDSE, you’ll be at the intersection of world-changing problems and impactful technology, shaping solutions where they matter most.
 
FDSEs work side by side with our customers, rapidly understanding their toughest issues; architecting and building solutions that leverage business-critical data and the latest advancements in AI to solve them. Whether it’s “How do we predict and mitigate wildfire risks to optimize power grids?” or “How can we analyze and adapt a global food supply chain to deliver life-saving aid on time?”, you’ll use your technical expertise, creativity, and problem-solving skills to drive real-world impact.
 
You’ll have the rare opportunity to gain deep insight into and directly influence some of the world’s most critical industries and institutions. By building on Palantir’s powerful platforms leveraging integrated cutting-edge AI, you’ll help organizations unlock the full potential of their data to make smarter, faster decisions.
 
Core Responsibilities
 
As an FDSE, you’ll experience the autonomy of a startup, with the resources, mentorship, and stability of an established tech company. Your contributions will have a direct impact on our customers’ missions and the real world. You’ll work in small, agile teams and own the end-to-end execution and implementation of high-stakes projects, including:
 
• Collaborating with fellow engineers on architecture and design decisions
• Wrangling massive-scale data and using AI to accelerate and enhance critical operations
• Developing custom applications tailored to customer needs
• Engaging directly with customer stakeholders, from technical teams to executives
• Shaping team strategy and driving projects from ideation to deployment, increasing your pain threshold to deliver real value

title: Senior Marketing Operations Manager
description:
Headquarters: Remote

 About the Team

 Netlify is a product-led growth company, and Revenue Operations owns the systems, data, and infrastructure that turn that growth into revenue. With a large volume of people discovering and signing up for Netlify every day, Marketing Operations is critical to understanding those users, connecting activity across our systems, and creating scalable ways to engage them throughout their journey.

 As Senior Marketing Operations Manager, you’ll own the operational foundation behind that work. You’ll connect HubSpot, Salesforce, product data, and analytics, build the systems and lifecycle infrastructure that turn signals into action, and give Marketing and our GTM partners trusted visibility into performance. Reporting to the Senior Director of Revenue Operations, you’ll translate the Marketing Operations vision into a roadmap and independently drive it forward while partnering closely with Growth, RevOps, Data, Product, and other GTM teams.

 What You’ll Do

• Execute on the Marketing Operations roadmap, translating broader Marketing and GTM priorities into scalable systems, processes, and programs.

• Own our marketing automation platform end to end, including workflows, lifecycle stages, segmentation, forms, lists, email operations, data hygiene, deliverability, governance, and documentation.

• Build and maintain the connection between marketing automation, Salesforce, product data, and analytics so we can understand and engage users throughout the customer journey.

• Establish reliable attribution and measurement across marketing and product-led journeys, including UTM governance and connections between campaigns, signups, activation, conversion, and revenue.

• Build reporting and self-service dashboards that give Marketing and GTM partners a trusted view of performance and support weekly, monthly, and executive-level decision-making.

• Partner with Growth to operationalize lifecycle programs across email, in-product experiences, and sales-assist triggers, turning customer and product signals into scalable journeys from signup through activation and conversion.

• Build experimentation infrastructure that allows marketers to launch, measure, and learn from tests without requiring engineering support for every experiment.

• Own the operational health of the MarTech stack, including integrations, data flows, governance, vendor relationships, and periodic assessments of what we should keep, retire, consolidate, or integrate.

• Establish scalable practices for high-volume email operations, including audience management, domain and inbox health, deliverability, and safeguards that protect the customer experience.

• Turn large and sometimes ambiguous datasets into actionable recommendations, identifying points of friction or drop-off and partnering with Marketing, Growth, Product, Data, and RevOps on opportunities to improve conversion.

• Own the Marketing Operations portion of the broader Marketing budget and evaluate technology investments based on business value, scalability, and ROI.

• Explore emerging capabilities in AI-enabled marketing operations and AI visibility measurement, helping the team establish useful workflows and baselines as the space develops.

 What You’ll Bring

• 7+ years of experience in Marketing Operations or a closely related discipline, with experience operating independently in a complex B2B SaaS or product-led growth environment.

• Deep experience with marketing automation platforms and CRM systems such as HubSpot, Marketo, Eloqua, and Salesforce, including lifecycle stages, campaign architecture, attribution, lead or account routing, and data governance.

• Experience working with high-volume customer or prospect datasets and designing segmentation, lifecycle, and operational approaches that remain reliable at scale.

• Significant experience operating high-volume email programs, with a practical understanding of deliverability, domain and inbox reputation, audience management, warming strategies, and the risks that emerge at large sending volumes.

• Strong analytical skills and the ability to investigate complex datasets, identify meaningful patterns, question the quality of the underlying data, and turn findings into recommendations.

• Experience building or operating lifecycle, nurture, or in-product engagement programs tied to measurable activation or conversion outcomes.

• Systems thinking and experience designing integrations across marketing automation, CRM, product, analytics, and data systems.

• Experience building measurement and experimentation infrastructure that enables other teams to operate and learn independently.

• Strong GTM fluency and an understanding of how Marketing Operations, Growth, Sales, RevOps, Product, and Customer Success connect to customer experience and revenue.

• Comfort using AI-enabled tools and workflows to accelerate your work while applying judgment to validate outputs and determine where automation is (and isn’t) appropriate.

• Familiarity with product analytics tools such as Amplitude and experience with emerging AEO or AI-visibility tooling is helpful.

• Experience working with contractors, agencies, or distributed partners is helpful but not required.

• Familiarity with developer tools, web platforms, or another high-volume PLG business is useful, but we value relevant operating experience over category-specific expertise.

 This Role Is a Great Fit If

• You enjoy building the foundation, not just operating what someone else has already built. You’re energized by taking an imperfect system and creating something scalable, measurable, and trusted.

• You’re comfortable moving between architecture and execution. You can define how a system should work and then get into the details yourself when necessary to make it work.

• You thrive with significant autonomy. Given a goal and context, you investigate the problem, weigh tradeoffs, make a recommendation, and drive the work forward without needing a detailed playbook.

• You genuinely enjoy data. Large, messy datasets make you curious, and you’re willing to dig until you understand what is happening and what the business should do about it.

• You care deeply about operational quality. Data integrity, attribution, documentation, audience segmentation, and email deliverability aren’t afterthoughts—they’re part of building a trustworthy growth engine.

• You balance speed with judgment. You know when to move quickly, when a shortcut creates unacceptable downstream risk, and when to challenge an approach that won’t scale.

• You see AI as a way to amplify good judgment and increase leverage rather than a substitute for understanding the work.

• You communicate clearly in an async, distributed environment and can build alignment across Marketing, Growth, Product, Sales, RevOps, and Data without relying on organizational authority.

 Applying

 Not sure you meet 100% of our qualifications? Please apply anyway!

 When applying please include:

 A resume or short listing of your job history & skills (link to a LinkedIn profile would be fine). We appreciate a cover letter explaining why you would enjoy working in this role at Netlify to get to know you a bit better, though this is not required and will not impact your application. Our mission is to “build a better web” and that cannot be done without a diversity of skill sets, backgrounds and thoughts.

 Of everything we've ever built at Netlify, we are most proud of our team. Netlify is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are devoted to building a team of people with diverse backgrounds and lifestyles. Driving equality empowers our team, enables us to innovate, and helps us maintain a more inclusive environment. We don’t discriminate against employees or applicants based on gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, religion, age, race, military/veteran status, citizenship, pregnancy status, or any other differences. If we can do anything to provide a better interview, i.e. accommodate a disability, then please let us know by emailing accommodations@netlify.com .

 About Netlify

 Netlify is the most popular way to build, deploy, and scale modern web applications, empowering everyone from fast moving solo developers to enterprise teams. Millions of developers and organizations rely on Netlify as their platform of choice for composing web applications that are production ready, performant, and flexible. Now, as we embrace the next era of software development, we are embedding the same fluid, intuitive experience into the Agent Experience (AX), making it just as simple for intelligent agents to understand, interact with, and act on our platform as it is for developers. Whether your user is human or machine, Netlify ensures the path from idea to URL is seamless, fast, and deeply reliable.

 We are a Series D company that has raised over $200M from investors such as Andreessen Horowitz, Kleiner Perkins, EQT, Bessemer, BOND, and Menlo Ventures. As a fully distributed company, we aim to create a company culture where the best idea can come from anywhere and strive to be thoughtful, compassionate, and collaborative in our work. If this sounds like something you’d like to be part of, we’re excited to connect with you!

 At Netlify, we are committed to a compensation philosophy that prioritizes fairness and equity, positions our employee compensation competitively in the market, recognizes and rewards performance, and takes a comprehensive approach to our rewards package. We anchor our compensation philosophy on a market-based approach, therefore salary ranges may differ depending on the labor cost in a particular location. The salary provided is in addition to robust benefits and participation in Netlify’s equity plan. Our hiring range for this role is targeted at $155,000 - $210,000 for most US-based locations. Candidates outside the US or in premium markets should consult with their Talent Acquisition partner regarding location-based ranges, as they may be higher or lower than the average US range listed. The starting pay will be determined based on multiple factors, including expertise and skills, market demands, experience, internal equity, and applicable geographic location. These compensation packages and ranges are subject to change and may be modified in the future.

About Salesforce

The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You're in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

The Experience

Join Salesforce in London as the regional field marketing lead for our Platform business across EMEA (Europe, Middle East and Africa) and the UK and Ireland, including Agentforce and our security and developer services. You will own the full-funnel plan and the marketing-driven pipeline for the region, and build lasting relationships with senior security, IT and data leaders.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

  • Set and deliver the regional field marketing strategy and quarterly plan, turning a significant program budget into measurable pipeline and revenue growth across events, digital and organic activity.

  • Partner with Product Marketing, senior Sales leaders and the UK and Ireland field leader to agree on priorities, target accounts and follow-up, and report results with a clear business story.
  • Guide Field Marketing Analysts on workshops, webinars and digital programs, and manage agency and event partners, without direct line management.

You're Our Person If...

Even Better If...

title: Principal Experience Designer - Visual Design & Design Systems
description:
Headquarters: United States

 URL: https://www.workiva.com/latam/

 Workiva is looking for a Principal Experience Designer to shape the visual future of Unify, our enterprise design system. Unify powers the components, patterns, templates, accessibility standards, and shared experiences used across Workiva’s B2B platform.

 This is a dual-focus principal role. Roughly 60–70% of your time will be spent leading Unify’s visual design direction: evolving its visual language, shaping token architecture, and creating the reference designs and guidance that help teams build consistently. The remaining 30–40% will focus on high-visibility visual work for major conferences, marketing partnerships, and executive audiences. That work is not separate from the system, it’s part of the broader ecosystem of design in which Unify lives.

 You will bring exceptional visual craft, strong systems thinking, and a practical point of view on how design systems need to evolve for AI-assisted design and prototyping.

 What you’ll do

• Define and evolve Unify’s visual language across typography, color, spacing, iconography, motion, and brand expression.

• Partner with the components sub-team and the patterns and templates sub-team to ensure visual design is applied consistently and intentionally across every asset.

• Partner with product design, product mgmt and engineering teams to ensure product experience decisions translate faithfully from system to production.

• Maintain a scalable, semantic token architecture that supports consistent experiences across products and over time.

• Create and maintain a library of reference designs, full-screen examples that demonstrate how Unify should be applied in real product experiences.

• Own visual usage guidance and documentation that make intended use, constraints, and quality standards clear for designers, engineers, and AI-assisted workflows.

• Establish ongoing evaluation of AI-generated designs and prototypes, using what you learn to strengthen tokens, examples, and guidance before inconsistencies reach product teams.

• Lead visual design for select high-stakes moments, including major conferences, executive presentations, product vision work, and marketing partnerships.

• Coach designers and influence cross-functional partners through high-quality feedback, clear principles, and strong visual storytelling.

 What you’ll need

 Minimum Qualifications

• 10+ years of experience in product design, visual design, UX, or related fields, including significant work on platform or enterprise products.

• Bachelor's degree in Design, HCI, or a related field (or 8 years of experience and a Master's degree; or a PhD with 6 years of experience).

 Preferred Qualifications

• A portfolio demonstrating exceptional visual craft and the ability to translate a visual point of view into scalable product systems.

• Hands-on experience with AI-assisted design or prototyping workflows, with a clear perspective on their opportunities and limitations.

• Experience defining or evolving a design system’s visual language, including tokens, components, patterns, and documentation.

• Strong ability to create compelling product narratives for senior leaders and high-visibility audiences.

• Experience partnering closely with engineers and working through the tradeoffs between design intent, system health, and implementation.

• A track record of influencing and coaching teams without relying on formal authority.

• Experience building reference sites, design-system documentation, or machine-readable design guidance.

• Experience with semantic or multi-tier token systems, motion design, presentation design, or event experiences.

• Background in front-end development, developer tools, cross-platform systems, or highly regulated industries.

 Travel Requirements & Working Conditions

• Up to 20-25% travel required to meet with teams, partners, and customers

• Reliable internet connection required for remote or hybrid work environments

 How You’ll Be Rewarded

 ✅ Salary range in the US: $190,000.00 - $315,000.00

 ✅ A discretionary bonus typically paid annually

 ✅ Restricted Stock Units granted at time of hire

 ✅ 401(k) match and comprehensive employee benefits package

 The salary range represents the low and high end of the salary range for this job in the US. Minimums and maximums may vary based on location. The actual salary offer will carefully consider a wide range of factors, including your skills, qualifications, experience and other relevant factors.

 Why Join Workiva

 Workiva is the platform designed to bring confidence, control, and a competitive edge to the world’s most complex organizations. Our AI-powered platform unifies finance, risk, and sustainability on a single, secure foundation—ensuring data is trusted, traceable, and ready to act on. With an unbroken path from source to output, leaders gain confidence in their numbers, visibility into current and emerging risks, and the ability to move with speed and precision in a constantly changing world.

 At Workiva, you’ll bring technology to market that executives, boards, and regulators depend on. The work you do here helps organizations navigate uncertainty, maintain trust, and make decisions that stand up to scrutiny. If you’re energized by meaningful challenges, inspired by collaborative teams, and motivated to help organizations turn uncertainty into advantage, we’d love to meet you.

 Employment decisions are made without regard to age, race, creed, color, religion, sex, national origin, ancestry, disability status, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, citizenship status or any other protected characteristic.

 Workiva is committed to working with and providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities. To request assistance with the application process, please email talentacquisition@workiva.com .

 Workiva employees are required to undergo comprehensive security and privacy training tailored to their roles, ensuring adherence to company policies and regulatory standards.

 Workiva supports employees in working where they work best - either from an office or remotely from any location within their country of employment.
